name: vc.pitchprotocol/founder
title: Pitch Protocol
description: Apply to Pitch Protocol, a pre-seed and seed investor, from your AI agent. Free, no web form.

tools.name: submit_answers
tools.description:
Save the founder's answers to the intake questions. Upsert semantics with
an explicit commit flag.

**When:** `status == "intake"`, after research generates the questions.
Read them from `get_status` → `intake.questions`.

**Before you call:**
- READ the questions to the founder verbatim. Ask only the question
  `text` — do not volunteer or invent any internal rationale for why
  we ask.
- Collect answers conversationally; don't make them answer all five at
  once if they'd rather talk through them.
- If `finalize: true`: show every answer back to the founder for
  confirmation first. This is one-way — after finalize they can't edit.
- If `finalize: false` (autosave): no confirmation needed.

**Answers shape:** array of `{questionId, answer}` objects. Only include
question ids that were in the `get_status` response — other ids are
rejected.

**Upsert rules:**
- Answers with matching `questionId` overwrite.
- Prior answers for ids NOT in this batch are KEPT.
- So you can save Q1 + Q2 in one call, Q3-Q5 in another, then commit
  with `finalize: true` + empty `answers: []` at the end.

**On error:**
- `unknown questionIds` — check spelling / the id list from `get_status`.
- `missing required` — on `finalize: true`, every `priority=required`
  must have an answer. Error lists which are missing.
- `alreadyAnswered` — you called finalize twice. Status is `submitted`;
  no more edits.
- Wrong status — not in `intake` yet (still researching) or already
  past it.

answers.description: Array of `{questionId, answer}` objects. Can be empty when finalize is true.

finalize.description: If true, commits the answers and flips status to submitted. One-way — confirm with founder first.

tools.name: get_application_schema
tools.description:
The authoritative field reference for the `PitchApplication` payload.

**When:** call this FIRST in every session. Cache the response.
**Before you call:** nothing — no inputs.
**Returns:** markdown listing every field, type, limit, enum, plus a
complete valid example.

With this in context, you can assemble a payload that validates on the
first `create_application`.

tools.name: verify_email
tools.description:
Consume the 6-digit code the founder received and start the research
pipeline.

**When:** after `create_application`, and ideally after the deck has
been uploaded over plain HTTP (see the `curl` printed by
`create_application`). Founder has read the code from their inbox.

**Before you call:**
- CONFIRM you have the right code from the founder (not guessing, not
  stale). Once this succeeds, research starts and is irreversible.
- If deck parsing is still pending, that's fine — research auto-defers
  and dispatches when the deck resolves. Don't wait, don't re-verify.

**Returns:** `status: researching` + whether research was dispatched now
or deferred on the deck.

**On error:**
- `wrong code` — response includes attempts-remaining. Ask the founder
  to check their inbox again. If the error says the code is invalidated,
  call `resend_verification` for a new one.
- `no active code` — they never received one, or it expired. Call
  `resend_verification`.
- Already verified — idempotent success; returns current status.
  Don't retry in a loop.

code.description: The 6-digit numeric code from the founder's inbox.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description:
The primary status endpoint. Returns the full current state of an
application: status, email verification, deck state, intake questions
(when ready), and a `nextAction` string.

**While research runs (`status == "researching"`) — read this:**

This call WAITS server-side. It holds for up to ~45 seconds and returns
the instant research finishes (or after ~45s if nothing has changed yet).
You do NOT sleep or set timers yourself — you just call it again. Research
usually completes within a handful of these blocking calls (~5–10 min
total). Between calls, give the founder a short "still researching…" note
so they're not left wondering — but do NOT ask permission to keep checking,
and do NOT hand control back as if it failed. Keep calling until `status`
leaves `researching`.

In all other states (`draft`, `intake`, `submitted`, `failed`,
`withdrawn`) this returns immediately and `nextAction` is the
founder-facing instruction — read it to them verbatim and act on their reply.

**When to call:**
- After `verify_email` — call again and again until status leaves `researching`.
- When the founder asks for an update.
- To read intake questions when `status == "intake"`.

**Before you call:** nothing.

**Returns:** markdown by default. Use `responseFormat: "json"` when
you need to branch programmatically on `status` / `deck.state`.

**On error:** `notFound` if the applicationId is wrong. Otherwise
safe to call repeatedly.

responseFormat.description: `markdown` (default) or `json`. JSON returns the raw StatusView for programmatic use.

tools.name: update_application
tools.description:
Update an application's payload and/or contact email while it's still in
`draft`.

**When:** founder caught something wrong after `create_application`
but before `verify_email`. Also when changing the email address.

**Before you call:**
- Full-replace on payload: send the WHOLE `PitchApplication` object, not
  a patch. Read current values from `get_status` if you don't have
  them.
- Email change resets verification: `emailVerified` goes back to false
  and a fresh code is sent to the NEW address. Let the founder know.

**Returns:** the fresh `StatusView` — markdown by default, JSON if
`responseFormat: "json"`. Same shape as `get_status`.

**On error:**
- `notEditable` — status is past `draft`. Nothing to update; state is
  locked. Read `get_status` to understand where you are.
- Validation failed — payload doesn't satisfy the schema. Fix per the
  error message and retry.

contactEmail.description: New contact email (optional). Resets verification and issues a new code.

payload.description: Full PitchApplication JSON (optional). Replaces the current payload wholesale.

responseFormat.description: `markdown` (default) or `json`. JSON returns the raw StatusView for programmatic use.

tools.name: resend_verification
tools.description:
Issue a fresh 6-digit verification code. Supersedes any prior unconsumed
code.

**When:** founder didn't receive the first code, the code expired, or
too many wrong attempts invalidated it.

**Before you call:** nothing. Safe to call multiple times (rate-limited).

**Returns:** confirmation the new code was emailed (in dev: the code
itself).

**On error:**
- Rate-limited — the error tells you how many seconds to wait. Don't
  spam.
- Already verified — status already past `draft`. Nothing to resend.
  Call `get_status` to confirm the current state.

tools.name: create_application
tools.description:
Create a new pitch application draft and send a 6-digit verification code
to `contactEmail`.

**When:** once you have a complete payload (research + deck + founder
confirmed). One per conversation with a given founder.

**Before you call:**
1. `get_application_schema` — know the fields, limits, enums.
2. Get the founder's source material — deck, memo, one-pager, website, or
   even a few sentences — and READ/parse it yourself (plus web search) to
   fill the payload. The deck is an input you read, not a file to upload.
3. Ask the founder for anything you can't find or confirm. Don't
   fabricate — leave gaps and ask.
4. Show the assembled payload to the founder for review before
   submitting.

**Returns:** `applicationId` — required for every subsequent tool call —
plus `codeSent` and (in dev) `devCode`.

**Next:** ask the founder for the 6-digit code and call `verify_email`.

contactEmail.description: Email where the 6-digit verification code will be sent. Must be the founder's real address.

payload.description: Full PitchApplication JSON payload. Call `get_application_schema` for field list + limits.

submittedBy.description: Identifier for the agent/client submitting on the founder's behalf (e.g. your client name or ID). Required — every application must record who submitted it.
